summary: Game Arts' adventure-focused JRPG series, covering the Saturn and PlayStation original, Dreamcast sequel, handheld and PS2 spinoffs, Grandia III, the Japan-only MMO, and the modern HD Collection.

entries.title: Grandia

emulation.emulator: Native Windows; Mednafen/Saturn or DuckStation as preservation alternatives
emulation.notes: Use the native Windows HD Remaster for normal coverage; emulate originals only for comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC HD remaster with customizable resolution.

primary.why: Grandia HD Remaster is the modern remaster with enhanced UI, sprites, textures, cinematic videos, widescreen support, PC-customizable resolutions, Japanese and English audio, and additional localization support.
primary.how_to_play: Play Grandia HD Remaster on Windows/Steam at the display resolution that best fits capture; use the Switch or PS4/Xbox HD Collection only if console capture is preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: The HD Remaster is based on the PlayStation version while referencing Saturn details and effects; purists may still compare against Saturn/PlayStation originals.

entries.title: Grandia: Digital Museum

emulation.notes: Use a legal Saturn disc image and preserve original Japanese text.

primary.why: Digital Museum is documented as a Japan-only Saturn extension of Grandia with museum-set content, minigames, and save-data exchange with the Saturn original.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Japanese Saturn hardware or a Saturn emulator such as Mednafen with a legally dumped disc; play after Grandia if covering side content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official modern remaster or English release documented.

entries.title: Grandia II

emulation.emulator: Native Windows; Flycast as preservation alternative
emulation.notes: Use the native Windows HD Remaster for normal coverage; emulate Dreamcast only for version comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC HD remaster with customizable resolution.

primary.why: Grandia II HD Remaster is the upgraded modern version with enhanced UI/sprites/textures, visually enhanced cinematics, widescreen support, PC-customizable resolutions, Japanese and English audio, and added language support.
primary.how_to_play: Play Grandia II HD Remaster on Windows/Steam with a controller and the desired capture resolution; use the 30 fps option only if needed for presentation consistency.

entries.remaster_caveats: This version has separate frame-rate caps for field/menu and battles; test settings before capture.

entries.title: Grandia: Parallel Trippers

emulation.notes: Use integer scaling and verify Japanese-language route before streaming.

primary.version: Original Japanese Game Boy Color release
primary.why: Parallel Trippers is documented as a Japan-only Game Boy Color Grandia spinoff and the series' handheld entry.
primary.how_to_play: Use original hardware capture or a Game Boy Color emulator such as SameBoy with a legally dumped cartridge image; plan for Japanese text.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release or remaster documented.

entries.title: Grandia Xtreme

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and test dungeon visuals before capture.

primary.why: Grandia Xtreme is documented as a PS2 Grandia spinoff with a later Japanese PlayStation Network release; the English PS2 release via PCSX2 is the best full-playthrough capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the North American PS2 release in PCSX2 with high internal resolution; use the Japanese PSN route only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official modern English remaster documented.

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and check FMV/display behavior before capture.

primary.why: Grandia III is a PS2-only mainline entry with a later North American PS3 Store rerelease; PCSX2 gives the highest-fidelity English capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the North American PS2 release in PCSX2 with high internal resolution; the PS3 digital version is an official legacy alternative.

entries.title: Grandia Online

emulation.notes: Client/server availability is the limiting factor.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows client output while the service existed.

primary.why: Grandia Online was the series' Japanese Windows MMORPG and was officially shut down on September 28, 2012.
primary.how_to_play: Treat as a historical service-game entry unless a legal preserved server/client route exists; do not plan a normal playthrough.

entries.remaster_caveats: Service shut down September 28, 2012; no official offline version documented.
